We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to another phenyl ring bearing an α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So overall: a sulfonamide linking two phenyls, and an amide side chain.

We need 3 steps retrosynthesis, using the hints: step 1 forward: amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). So retrosynthetic step: break amide bond to give carboxylic acid and amine.

Step 2 forward: Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (with decarboxylation). So retrosynthetic step: break the C=C double bond and the carboxylic acid to give aromatic aldehyde and malonic acid? Actually forward: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid. So reverse: from α,β-unsaturated acid, we can get aldehyde + malonic acid. In our target, the unsaturated chain is /C=C/C(=O)N... The α,β-unsaturated acid would be after hydrolysis of amide? Wait the unsaturated part is attached to carbonyl amide: /C=C/C(=O)N... So the α,β-unsaturated acid would be /C=C/COOH. So we need to break amide first to get acid, then break double bond to get aldehyde + malonic acid.

Step 3 forward: sulfonamide formation from amine + sulfonyl chloride. So retrosynthetic step: break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonyl fluoride) and amine.

Thus route: target -> (1) disconnect amide: give α,β-unsaturated acid (same chain but COOH) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). (2) disconnect α,β-unsaturated acid via Doebner: give aromatic aldehyde (the phenyl ring bearing sulfonamide) and malonic acid. (3) disconnect sulfonamide: give sulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride) and the aromatic amine (the same phenyl ring with amine? Actually the sulfonamide attaches to the first phenyl (para-methyl phenyl) via N-SO2- to the second phenyl (the one bearing the unsaturated chain). In target, the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the first phenyl (para-methyl phenyl) and the sulfonyl attached to second phenyl. So breaking gives sulfonyl chloride attached to second phenyl (i.e., 4-(sulfonyl chloride) phenyl) and the first phenyl amine (p-toluidine). So final precursors: p-toluidine (para-methyl aniline), 4-(chlorosulfonyl)phenyl (or sulfonyl chloride) with aldehyde substituent? Wait the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the second phenyl which also has the aldehyde substituent (the aldehyde that will undergo Doebner). So the sulfonyl chloride precursor is 4-(chlorosulfonyl)benzaldehyde (or with aldehyde at para to sulfonyl?). In target, the second phenyl has the unsaturated chain at para position relative to sulfonyl? Let's examine SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to S(=O)(=O)N- (the N attached to first phenyl). So the sulfonyl is attached to the second phenyl at position 1 (the sulfonyl attached to N). The aromatic ring has the unsaturated amide at para position? The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. That's a phenyl with substituent at position 1 (connected to sulfonyl) and at position 4 (the unsaturated chain). So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be 4-formyl-phenylsulfonyl chloride? Actually the aldehyde is at para to sulfonyl. So we need 4-formylbenzenesulfonyl chloride.

Thus retrosynthesis:

Step 1 (amide formation): target -> precursor A (α,β-unsaturated acid attached to phenyl) + aniline (c3ccccc3N). The α,β-unsaturated acid is: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1? Wait after amide cleavage, we have COOH instead of CONH-PhNH2. So product: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1 (the acid). That's the unsaturated acid.

Step 2 (Doebner): unsaturated acid -> aldehyde (4-formyl phenyl sulfonyl) + malonic acid. So precursor B: 4-formylbenzenesulfonyl chloride? Actually we need sulfonyl chloride later, but step 2 gives aldehyde attached to sulfonyl? The sulfonyl is part of the aromatic ring; we haven't broken sulfonamide yet. So after step 2, we have aromatic aldehyde with sulfonyl group (maybe sulfonyl chloride). But Doebner uses aldehyde (aryl aldehyde) + malonic acid to give α,β-unsaturated acid attached to same aryl. So the aryl must have sulfonyl group already attached (as sulfonyl chloride). So the aldehyde precursor is 4-formylbenzenesulfonyl chloride (or sulfonyl chloride). So step 2: unsaturated acid -> 4-formylbenzenesulfonyl chloride + malonic acid.

Step 3 (sulfonamide formation): 4-formylbenzenesulfonyl chloride + p-toluidine -> sulfonamide intermediate (aryl sulfonyl chloride + aniline). Then after step 2? Wait order: In forward synthesis, you would first form sulfonamide (step 3 forward) then Doebner (step 2 forward) then amide coupling (step 1 forward). But retrosynthesis order is reverse: target -> break amide -> unsaturated acid -> break unsat via Doebner -> aldehyde + malonic acid -> break sulfonamide -> sulfonyl chloride + p-toluidine.

Thus final precursors: p-toluidine (para-methyl aniline), 4-formylbenzenesulfonyl chloride, malonic acid.

Maybe need to specify functional_groups_broken: "aliphatic carboxylic acid" and functional_groups_formed: "amide". That gave empty. Could be that the database uses "carboxylic acid" not "aliphatic".
